conclusion: Property 6 is VACUOUS: in box A, the rectangle chosen and committed in advance precisely because it contains the pinned Davenport-Heilbronn off-line zero and is therefore the box most favourable to a DISTINGUISHES verdict, the Epstein zeta of the non-principal discriminant -23 form has no zeros and so satisfies the property exactly as zeta does. The larger finding is that property 6 is not well posed as a gate input at all, since box A and box B assign opposite truth values to the same function; quantified over all boxes it is RH restricted to a region and so unknowable for zeta, and instantiated on any affordable box it is vacuous.
confidence: The VACUOUS verdict is float-grade, one route, one resolution. Two controls with known answers passed (a straddling box on xi returning 1 at gamma_1, and the Davenport-Heilbronn box A cell returning the pinned zero), and the decisive count of 0 passed count_zeros_box's own guard, which forces every boundary segment under about 1/8 of a phase turn before adaptive refinement and refuses a winding residual above 1e-6. But the planned reconfirmation at halved and quartered step did NOT complete: both re-counts hit the 420 s cap, so the decisive cell has not been checked at a finer resolution and this is the weakest joint in the result. The verdict is nonetheless hard to move, because the box B row for the Davenport-Heilbronn function is a second, cheap, independently-computed survivor (0.24 s) and one survivor settles a box under the battery's own rule. Lean less on the proposed box-free replacement: its zeta half is a theorem, but its rivals half is the 1936 Davenport-Heilbronn theorem quoted from the literature and not witnessed in this tree.

threads.what: The battery's property-6 column is not literally the same claim across the four functions: zeta.epstein.dh_interface wires count_zeros_box to the uncompleted dh_f, while zeta_interface uses xi and epstein_interface uses epstein_completed.
threads.why_it_might_matter: Harmless in every box used here, because the gamma factor of completed_dh is finite and non-vanishing there, so nothing in this hunt is affected. But the gamma factor has poles at s = -1, -3, -5, ..., so any box reaching into Re s < 0 would have the four columns counting different objects while reporting one verdict.
threads.first_step: Open an issue on zeta-lab; the one-line fix is to point dh_interface's count_zeros_box at completed_dh, with a test on a box straddling s = -1 that fails under the current wiring.

threads.what: count_zeros_box's default step is derived from the phase-turn rate of the Davenport-Heilbronn function and appears to be the wrong scale for the Epstein zetas: the two discriminant -23 forms cost the same per evaluation (0.9895 s and 1.0154 s), yet one finished box A in 29 s and the other did not finish in 420 s, and halving the step turned the 29 s count into a cap hit.
threads.why_it_might_matter: Since the forced subdivision count is identical for both forms, the blowup is in the adaptive refinement, which means the Epstein phase is turning far faster along those edges than the heuristic assumes. Three of this hunt's eight cells are empty for this reason, and it is what made the previous 50-minute attempt unaffordable too.
threads.first_step: Instrument _arg_variation to count evaluations per edge for (2,1,3) on box A, then try a step derived from the Epstein zero density rather than from 5t/2pi.

threads.what: No witness in this tree for a zero with Re s > 1 of any of the three rivals, though the 1936 Davenport-Heilbronn theorem says all three have infinitely many.
threads.why_it_might_matter: It is the missing half of the box-free replacement property this hunt proposes. This repository normally requires that a claim it leans on be measured here rather than quoted, and the module's own docstring already flags the Epstein off-line zeros as quoted and not recomputed.
threads.first_step: Run the argument-principle count over a tall thin box in Re s > 1 for the Davenport-Heilbronn function first, since it is the cheapest of the three; hunts/gate5_p6_a/probe.py already carries that box as box C.

threads.what: A gate input whose zeta column is unknowable is not a gate input, and the battery has no admission rule saying so.
threads.why_it_might_matter: Property 6 spent a previous 50-minute attempt and this one before the ill-posedness was named. Three of the six battery properties came back vacuous; a stated admission rule would have caught this one before any compute was spent on it.
threads.first_step: Propose to docs/09 that a candidate gate #3 property must state, before it is run, what makes its zeta column decidable without assuming RH.

core_candidates.what: A wall-clock-capped cell runner for battery-style tables, where a cell that overruns is recorded as a named gap rather than being allowed to kill the run or, worse, to be read as a truth value.
core_candidates.why_reusable: The previous attempt at this exact question died at 50 minutes with nothing written down. This run hit the same wall twice and still produced a settled verdict, purely because each cell had its own cap and results were saved incrementally. Any comparison across functions of wildly different cost has this shape.
core_candidates.first_step: Lift the count/save/cap loop out of hunts/gate5_p6_a/probe.py into a small helper once a second hunt needs it; do not build it before that.

core_candidates.what: A preregistration convention that commits the parameter file one commit before the probe file exists, so the commit order is the evidence that the parameters were not chosen on the answer.
core_candidates.why_reusable: It cost nothing here (one extra commit) and it is what makes an adversarially-chosen box readable as adversarial rather than as shopping. It generalizes to any hunt whose verdict depends on a free parameter.
core_candidates.first_step: If Fulcrum wants it enforced rather than practised, a test could assert that a hunt's MISSION.md commit predates its probe.py commit; that is a review-discipline question, so it is reported and not built.

notes_for_operator: Two things belong to Fulcrum rather than to the science and are named here in one line each rather than acted on. First, the cost asymmetry between the two Epstein forms is a budgeting fact for any future run against this module, not just a defect report. Second, this hunt was launched as one of three independent attacks on the same question; I did not look at the other branches or hunt directories, and the comparison across the three is the operator's measurement to make, not mine. The prepare-commit-msg telemetry hook was not installed in this fresh clone, so the preregistration commit 14dbb17 carries no Run-Id trailer; I installed the hook and put the trailer on later commits by hand rather than rewrite the commit whose ordering is the evidence. One process note that is mine and not Fulcrum's: my --confirm invocation raced the main run and overwrote results.json with a stale copy. The full cell table was restored from a snapshot taken before the overwrite, probe.py now re-reads before writing, and results.json records the incident in its run_notes.
